US-119-S5607.title: Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Clarification Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5607.description: A bill to amend the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 to restore the full 75-percent payment to counties from the Oregon and California land-grant fund, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5607.aiSummary: The bill would change the Secure Rural Schools law to restore the full 75% payment to counties from the Oregon and California land-grant fund. It would also update the law’s wording and payment names for forest and Bureau of Land Management land. The bill would spell out more election options for counties and states on which payments to receive.

US-119-S5508.title: Telecommunications Cybersecurity and Resilience Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5508.description: A bill to establish a public-private working group to develop cybersecurity best practices for telecommunications carriers and related supply chain participants, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5508.aiSummary: The bill would create a public-private working group within the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to develop cybersecurity best practices for telecommunications carriers and related supply chain companies. It would also set up a process for third-party assessors to certify use of those practices and require the group to share guidance and other materials. The best practices would be voluntary and focused on finding, stopping, reducing, and fixing cyber risks in the telecom sector.

US-119-HR2805.title: PLAN for Broadband Act
US-119-HR2805.summary:
Proper Leadership to Align Networks for Broadband Act or the PLAN for Broadband Act

This bill requires the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to develop and implement a national strategy to improve the coordination and management of federal broadband programs to meet the goal of providing high-speed, affordable broadband internet access services to all individuals in the United States. The strategy must also address barriers, costs, and administrative burdens for state, local, and tribal governments participating in these programs.

The NTIA must also develop and publish for public comment a plan for the implementation of the national strategy. Among other requirements, the implementation plan must (1) describe the roles and responsibilities of relevant agencies and interagency mechanisms, and (2) provide a plan for holding agencies accountable for objectives identified in the strategy.

The NTIA must submit the strategy and implementation plan to Congress and must periodically brief Congress on implementation progress.

Finally, the Government Accountability Office must submit a report to Congress that assesses the efficacy of the strategy and implementation plan and makes recommendations for improving them.

US-119-S4914.title: Green Ribbon Act of 2026
US-119-S4914.summary:
Green Ribbon Act of 2026

This bill provides statutory authority for and expands the Department of Education’s (ED’s) Green Ribbon Schools program. (This program was established in 2011 to recognize early learning centers, schools, districts, and postsecondary institutions for excellence in reducing environmental impact, increasing health and wellness, and providing sustainability education.)

In conducting the Green Ribbon Schools program, ED must (1) reserve funding for the Department of the Interior to carry out activities with respect to schools operated or funded by the Bureau of Indian Education; (2) award grants to state educational agencies for the purpose of supporting and engaging eligible entities as green schools; and (3) provide an honorarium to each award winner, subject to appropriations.

The bill directs the Institute of Museum and Library Services to establish an award program for nonformal learning institutions (e.g., libraries, museums, and zoos) that is modeled on ED’s program.

The bill also establishes within ED the Office of School Infrastructure and Sustainability.

US-119-S4914.aiSummary: The bill would expand the Green Ribbon Schools program at the Education Department, which recognizes schools and other learning centers for cutting environmental impact, improving health and wellness, and teaching about sustainability. It would set aside money for the Interior Department to work with schools run by the Bureau of Indian Education, give grants to state education agencies to support green schools, and provide a cash award to winners if money is approved. It would also create a similar award program for libraries, museums, zoos, and other non-school learning places, and set up a new office in the Education Department focused on school buildings and sustainability.

US-119-HR1815.title: VA Home Loan Program Reform Act
US-119-HR1815.summary:
VA Home Loan Program Reform Act

This act authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to take certain actions in cases of default on home loans under the VA home loan program, establishes a partial claim program, and temporarily increases amounts authorized for transitional housing and supportive services for veterans who are experiencing homelessness.

First, the act authorizes the VA to pay the holder of a loan guaranteed by the VA an amount necessary to avoid the foreclosure of the loan, provided that the holder of the loan and the veteran obligated on the loan execute documents to ensure the VA obtains a secured interest in the property covered by the loan.

The VA must prescribe loss mitigation procedures to help prevent the foreclosure of such a home loan. The VA may not take specified administrative actions (e.g., consent to the modification of loan terms) until the sequence of mitigation options has been completed.

Next, the act establishes a five-year Partial Claim Program under which the VA may make a partial claim (purchase a portion of the indebtedness) on VA loans for primary residences that are in default or at imminent risk of default. Individuals who default on loans for which the VA has made a partial claim under this program must be liable to the VA for any loss resulting from the default.

Further, the VA must report to Congress on its strategy to ensure that veterans who purchase homes under the VA home loan program are not at a disadvantage when attempting to secure representation by a real estate agent or broker.

Finally, the act temporarily increases the amounts authorized for the VA’s Grant and Per Diem program for FY2025 and FY2026. (The program provides funding to public or nonprofit private entities that provide housing and supportive services to veterans experiencing homelessness.)

US-119-HR1815.aiSummary: This law changes the VA home loan program so the Department of Veterans Affairs can help avoid foreclosure on some VA-backed home loans. It creates a five-year partial claim program, which lets the VA cover part of a loan balance for some primary homes that are in default or at risk of default. It also requires the VA to report to Congress on access to real estate agents or brokers for veteran home buyers and temporarily raises funding for housing and support services for homeless veterans in fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
